column3: the Beta-Bernoulli expected-loss comparison P(theta_b > theta_a) can be evaluated in bounded fixed-point integer arithmetic by iterating its exact term recurrence at a large scale, so no arbitrary-precision rationals are needed
column4: DISPROVEN BY MEASUREMENT, and the failure is silent rather than loud. A u128 fixed-point implementation at scale 1e24 returns exactly 0 ppm for ordinary parameter sizes -- not an inaccurate answer but a confidently wrong one, and 0 ppm reads as the candidate policy NEVER beats the fallback, which would pin a controller to its fallback permanently while looking like evidence. The closed form and its recurrence are exact and correct; it is the fixed-point EVALUATION that fails. Recorded because the approach is the obvious one and looks sound: the recurrence is factorial-free, every factor is a small rational, and nothing in it suggests underflow.
column5: The series spans more dynamic range than any fixed scale can hold. Measured T0 against the exact rational value: Beta(3,4) vs Beta(5,2) gives T0=3.571e-01; Beta(101,101) vs Beta(151,51) gives 7.166e-14; Beta(501,501) vs Beta(601,401) gives 2.955e-96; Beta(1001,1001) vs Beta(1501,501) gives 1.169e-129. The PEAK term is ~1e-2 in every case, so the series starts negligibly small and grows, spanning ~127 orders of magnitude between first term and peak while u128 offers ~38 decimal digits. T0 truncates to 0 at scale 1e24 and every later term is 0*ratio=0. Exact-rational evaluation agrees with numerical integration on four parameter sets including the symmetric control Beta(2,2) vs Beta(3,3) = 500000 ppm exactly, so the mathematics is not in question.
column6: someone implements either a mantissa-plus-exponent representation (which is reinventing floating point and needs its own constitutional argument), or arbitrary-precision rationals (no admitted crate provides them), or restructures the summation to begin at the peak term and work outward so no value near T0 is ever represented -- the last is plausible and unanalysed

column3: the four read modes (Current, BoundedStale, Snapshot, Offline) are distinguishable from one another by served-read latency, so a per-mode latency ordering is a reportable result
column4: REJECTED at this sample size on this host. The measured spread BETWEEN modes on one cell was 6-13 ms (medians: current 76.6, bounded_stale 81.2, snapshot 70.7, offline 68.2). The A/A noise floor measured on the SAME configurations -- identical state, mode and cell count, sampled twice back to back through the identical function in one process -- was 3.1 to 33.7 ms. The mode-to-mode differences are the same size as or smaller than the host's own run-to-run variation, so no ordering is supported. fgit-slo therefore reports per-mode medians beside the floor that makes them interpretable and asserts NO ordering; the e2e suite deliberately gates on exact counts only. The tempting claim this rejects is specific: 'Offline is cheapest because it makes no currentness claim' has a plausible mechanism and tidy numbers, and an unguarded measurement would have confirmed it

column3: aggregate read throughput on this substrate can be measured precisely enough to locate a stable saturation point and support a capacity model
column4: REJECTED on this host. Two sweeps of the identical code, twenty minutes apart, reported saturation at concurrency 8 (200 reads per reader per level: 40) and at concurrency 2 (200 reads per reader). Within the second sweep, two IDENTICAL back-to-back measurements at concurrency 2 returned 95 and 15 ops/s, and at concurrency 4 returned 7 and 93 ops/s -- spreads of 6.3x and 13x between arms that differ in nothing. Raising the sample count fivefold did not reduce the spread; the longer measurement window is more exposed to other panes' build bursts, not less, because the interference is non-stationary rather than independent jitter that averaging would cancel. Cause is not attributed between sample size and changing host load -- the two sweeps were not simultaneous, so that comparison cannot separate them -- but the consequence does not depend on which it is: the saturation point is determined by host interference rather than by the system under test, so no capacity model fitted to these points would be validated by them. The harness itself is sound throughout: all_offered_reads_served stayed true at every level of both sweeps, so the counts are exact and only the RATES move
